title: Python Conditional Expressions (Ternary Expressions)
learningObjectives: Explain how python conditional expressions (ternary expressions) control program flow.
Predict which branch executes for given inputs.
Apply conditions to practical decision tasks.
Choose readable alternatives when control flow becomes complex.

understand.concept: A conditional expression chooses one of two values using the form value_if_true if condition else value_if_false. It is an expression, so its result can be assigned, returned or passed to a function. Use it for short, simple choices; a regular if/else statement is clearer for multi-step branches.
understand.whyItMatters: A conditional expression provides a concise way to select a value based on a condition.
understand.analogy: It is like choosing one of two labels based on a yes-or-no question.
understand.analogyLimit: Nested conditional expressions can become difficult to read. Concision should not replace clarity.

explain.narrative:
## 1. Conditional expression form

The syntax is `result = A if condition else B`. Python evaluates the condition and then evaluates only the selected value expression.

## 2. Use it to choose a value

Conditional expressions are useful for short labels, defaults and simple calculations.

## 3. Prefer statements for complex work

If each branch needs several statements, use a normal if/else statement instead.

examples.title: Choose a simple label
examples.code:
age = 20
label = 'Adult' if age >= 18 else 'Minor'
print(label)
examples.explanation: The condition is true, so the first value is selected.

examples.title: Select a minimum
examples.code:
a = 8
b = 5
smallest = a if a < b else b
print(smallest)
examples.explanation: The expression chooses a when a is smaller, otherwise b.

examples.title: Choose a fallback message
examples.code:
name = ''
message = name if name else 'Guest'
print(message)
examples.explanation: An empty string is falsey, so the fallback value is selected.

examples.title: Use in a function argument
examples.explanation: The conditional expression supplies one string argument to print.

examples.title: Only the selected expression runs
examples.code:
ready = False
result = 'Go' if ready else 'Wait'
print(result)
examples.explanation: Only the else value expression is evaluated because ready is false.

practise.guidedTask: Use a conditional expression to choose a label based on a numeric threshold.
practise.independentTask: Choose the larger of two numbers and create a fallback display name for an empty string. Rewrite one example with if/else statements.
hints: Put the true value before if.
Use else to supply the false value.
The expression returns one selected value.
Use statements when branches need multiple actions.
practise.challenge: Compare a nested conditional expression with an equivalent if/elif/else statement and explain which is easier to maintain.

questions.prompt: Which is the correct conditional expression form?
options: if condition then A else B
questions.explanation: Python places the true value before if and the false value after else.

questions.prompt: What does a conditional expression produce?
questions.explanation: It is an expression that evaluates to one of two values.

questions.prompt: When should a regular if/else statement be preferred?
questions.explanation: Statements are clearer for multi-step branch bodies.

questions.prompt: In A if condition else B, when is A selected?
options: Only when A is a number
questions.explanation: The first value is selected when the condition is true.

questions.prompt: Which expression selects 'Guest' for an empty name?
questions.explanation: When name is empty, the condition is false and the else value is selected.
